text: The \(u\)-part. For \(i<j\), \(q_{ij}Y_it_j+Y_jt_i=q_{ij}\binom{d(i)}3\theta_{ij}t_i^2-\binom{d(j)}3\theta_{ij}t_j^2\); by (C\(_1\)), \(d(i)\mid u_{ij}q_{ij}\binom{d(i)}3\), and by (C\(_3\)), \(d(i)\mid u_{ij}\binom{d(j)}3\) (the \(w\)-terms of (C\(_1\)), (C\(_3\)) drop out, as \(d(i)\mid\binom{d(i)}2\) and \(d(i)\mid d(j)\mid\binom{d(j)}2\)); moreover \(d(i)\theta_{ij}t_i^2=0\) by Lemma 1, and \(d(i)\theta_{ij}t_j^2=0\) by applying \(t_j^2\) to \(Y_it_j=d(i)\theta_{ij}+\binom{d(i)}3\theta_{ij}t_i^2\) (as \(Y_it_j^3=0\)). So \(u_{ij}q_{ij}Y_it_j=-u_{ij}Y_jt_i\) and \(2U=-\sum_iZ_it_i\) with \(Z_i=\sum_{h>i}u_{ih}Y_h-\sum_{h<i}u_{hi}q_{hi}Y_h\). Writing \(Y_h=\sum_kb_{hk}x_{2k}+\sum_lc_{hl}x_{3l}\) modulo \(\gamma_4\) and using (B) and \(e(k)x_{2k}\equiv\sum_ld_{kl}x_{3l}\), one gets \(Z_it_i=\sum_l\rho_{il}\,x_{3l}t_i\) with \(\rho_{il}=\sum_{h>i}u_{ih}c_{hl}-\sum_{h<i}u_{hi}q_{hi}c_{hl}-\sum_kv'_{ik}d_{kl}\), since \(d(i)A\,t_i=0\) by Lemma 1. Condition (E) gives \(\rho_{il}\equiv\sigma_{il}\pmod{\gcd(d(i),f(l))}\), where \(\sigma_{il}\) collects the terms with \(\alpha\); the modulus kills \(x_{3l}t_i\) (\(f(l)x_{3l}\in\gamma_4\), and \(d(i)x_{3l}t_i=0\) by Lemma 1), and \(\sum_l\alpha^{(gh)}_lx_{3l}\equiv Y_gt_h\). So \(Z_it_i\) is a sum of terms \(u_{hi}q_{hi}Y_ht_i^2\) (\(h<i\)), \(w_{gih}Y_gt_ht_i\) (\(g\le i\le h\)), \(w_{ghi}Y_gt_ht_i\) (\(g\le h\le i\)) and \(w'_{igh}Y_gt_ht_i\) (\(i<g\le h\)), each zero: \(q_{hi}Y_ht_i^2=q_{hi}d(h)\theta_{hi}t_i=d(i)\theta_{hi}t_i=0\); for \(g<i\), \(Y_gt_ht_i=Y_gt_it_h=d(g)\theta_{gi}t_h\) with \(d(i)\mid w_{gih}d(g)\) and \(d(i)\theta_{gi}t_h=0\), while \(Y_it_i=0\) for \(g=i\); similarly \(d(h)\mid w_{ghi}d(g)\) and \(d(h)\theta_{gh}t_i=0\) for \(g<h\); and \(Y_gt_it_h=0\) for \(i<g\). Hence \(2U=0\), \(U=0\) as \(p\) is odd, \(g=1\), and \(D_5(Q)=1\) by [Tah81, Thm. 6.1].

Only (A\(_3\)), (A\(_4\)), (B), (C\(_1\)), (C\(_3\)), (E) are used (in the lattice computation below, dropping (E) changes the answer for one group, while the controls for the other five conditions are empty); oddness enters through Lemma 1, \(d\mid\binom d2\) and the final division by \(2\) (for \(p=2\) the identities fail). The step \(2U=-\sum_iZ_it_i\) is the analogue of \(w^2\equiv\prod_k[x_k,y_k]\) in [GT85, p. 132]. By computation (code: compute/magnus/m445): the identities hold in \(170\) random metabelian \(3\)-groups of class \(4\) (\(111\) with \(\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)\ge9\)) and in \(51\) metabelian \(5\)-groups, and fail in non-metabelian groups and for \(p=2\); in \(93\) metabelian groups every family of the whole lattice of admissible families gives \(g=1\); and \(112\) metabelian groups of class \(4\) with \(\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)\ge9\) have \(D_5=1\) in the truncated Magnus algebra.
